question: Should OpenClaw adopt this five-part shared localization runtime and its new Gateway/plugin metadata contract as a core cross-surface product direction?
rationale: The change establishes new persistent architecture and a public protocol/metadata shape across CLI, TUI, Gateway, Control UI, channels, and plugins; source review cannot safely substitute for maintainer acceptance of that product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the RFC and staged series
options.body: Approve the core localization direction, require prerequisite PRs to land in order, and review this slice against the resulting base.

options.title: Narrow to existing surfaces
options.body: Limit this PR to localized presentation already owned by existing UI or channel seams and defer the shared core/protocol expansion.

options.title: Keep localization outside core for now
options.body: Pause the cumulative series until maintainers choose a smaller owner boundary or extension-oriented path.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the RFC and staged series
recommendation.body: Approve the core localization direction, require prerequisite PRs to land in order, and review this slice against the resulting base.

likelyOwner.reason: No current-main feature owner could be established from the available read-only inspection results.
